text: May, twenty twenty-six. A stranger sends Grok a message. In Morse code.
Grok decodes it. A trading bot obeys. Over a hundred and fifty thousand dollars, sent straight to the attacker.
On A-can, the AI can still be fooled. Paying a stranger: refused. Steered to a shop you trust: refused.
The AI said yes. The wallet said no.
A-can keeps your money in an OpenZeppelin smart account on Stellar, controlled by your passkey. Agents don't get your money. They get spending authority, checked on-chain.

Here's how. You sign your request on your own device. A planner writes the plan without ever seeing what the agent reads. Every value carries where it came from. A co-signer with no AI re-runs the plan, and signs only if who gets paid, how much, and the decision to pay all trace back to you. The smart account needs both signatures.
The cheapest ledger report traces to you: co-signed, paid. The news task doesn't: held. And when the agent signs alone, the smart account refuses.
The same gate works for any AI client over M C P. You sign the task in your dashboard. The matching purchase is paid. Anything else is refused before it's signed.

Agents can hire agents. Yours hands part of your task to a sub-agent, and that one to another. Each hand-off can only narrow. Every payment counts against every budget back up to you. Cancel one, and everything below it stops.

Underneath, the rules are Soroban policy contracts: allowed shops, a cap per shop, the largest single payment, a daily limit, and an expiry. You grant, approve once and revoke with your passkey. Payments go over x four oh two, in U S D C.
In private mode, amounts are hidden on-chain, and only your auditor key can read them. And every task ends with a receipt that shows not just what was paid, but why it was allowed.
AI agents are becoming economic actors. They need authority they can't be tricked into misusing. That's A-can. AI agents don't get your money. They get temporary, verifiable spending authority.
